title: Arabic bedroom labels
goal: A reader must be able to read the Arabic room and furniture labels naturally and identify the door, window, and dimensions of a small bedroom.

rubric.must: The Arabic room name and furniture labels read naturally from right to left, with the room name's words in the correct order and no reversed letters or mirrored glyphs.
Arabic letters use their normal contextual joined forms wherever Arabic spelling permits joining, with no words rendered as a sequence of isolated letters.
The Arabic room name fits inside the room, and all three Arabic furniture labels fit within their respective furniture outlines without clipping or overlapping symbol strokes.
The room has an Arabic bedroom name, and the bed, wardrobe, and table each carry the appropriate ordinary Arabic name for that object.
The drawing shows one rectangular room dimensioned 3 by 4 metres with exactly three furniture pieces, all inside its walls and clear of the door swing.
One door has a visible leaf and inward swing arc at a wall opening, and one window has visible glazing lines in a separate wall opening.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the floorplan exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents one 3.00 m by 4.00 m bedroom with readable, correctly joined Arabic labels, exactly three labeled furniture pieces, an inward-swinging door, and a window with visible glazing lines.

items.evidence: The room label "غرفة نوم" and furniture labels "سرير", "خزانة", and "طاولة" read naturally right to left with correctly oriented glyphs.
All visible Arabic words use normal contextual joined letterforms rather than isolated characters.
The bedroom name fits within the room, and each furniture label is visibly contained within its respective bed, wardrobe, or table outline without clipping or stroke overlap.
The room is labeled "غرفة نوم"; the bed, wardrobe, and table are appropriately labeled "سرير", "خزانة", and "طاولة".
One rectangular room is dimensioned 3.00 by 4.00 metres and contains exactly three furniture pieces, all within the walls and clear of the door swing.
The south-wall door has a visible leaf and inward swing arc, while the north-wall window occupies a separate opening and has visible glazing lines.
